high_level_overview.overview: This program operates within a card transaction management system (CardDemo), serving as a batch maintenance utility for the Transaction Type reference table. It is part of the business logic layer responsible for keeping transaction classification data current and accurate. The program reads a sequential input file containing maintenance instructions and applies the corresponding database changes — inserts, updates, or deletions — to the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table in DB2. It solves the problem of bulk-maintaining transaction type reference data without requiring manual, record-by-record intervention, enabling administrators to submit a batch file of changes to be processed automatically.

key_features.description: Reads a sequential input file containing one or more transaction type maintenance records, processing each in turn until end-of-file is reached.
Evaluates each input record's type indicator (A, U, D, or *) to route processing to the appropriate add, update, delete, or skip operation.
Adds a new transaction type record to the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table using the transaction number and description from the input record.
Modifies the description of an existing transaction type record identified by its transaction number in the database.
Removes a transaction type record from the database based on the transaction number provided in the input file.
Recognizes lines prefixed with '*' as comments and skips them without performing any database operation, allowing annotated input files.

Captures and evaluates DB2 SQLCODE after each database operation, distinguishing between successful execution, not-found conditions, and hard errors, and triggers an abend routine with a descriptive message on failure.
On encountering invalid input types or database errors, sets a return code of 4 and displays an error message, signaling an abnormal condition to the calling environment.

input_output.name: INPFILE (TR-RECORD)
input_output.description: Sequential input file containing transaction type records. Each record includes a type indicator (A=Add, U=Update, D=Delete, *=Comment), a transaction type number (2 chars), and a transaction description (50 chars). The program reads all records sequentially to determine which database operation to perform.

input_output.name: CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE
input_output.description: DB2 database table storing transaction type definitions with columns TR_TYPE (CHAR 2) and TR_DESCRIPTION (VARCHAR 50). The program inserts new records (type A), updates existing descriptions by TR_TYPE key (type U), and deletes records by TR_TYPE key (type D) based on input file directives.

data_flow.description: Opens the sequential input file TR-RECORD (assigned to INPFILE) and checks file status for successful open
Reads the first record from the sequential input file into WS-INPUT-REC before entering the main processing loop
Inspects INPUT-REC-TYPE field to determine the operation to perform: 'A' for insert, 'U' for update, 'D' for delete, '*' to skip commented lines, or abend on invalid type
When INPUT-REC-TYPE is 'A', executes a DB2 INSERT into CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE using TR_TYPE and TR_DESCRIPTION values from the input record. Abends on negative SQLCODE.
When INPUT-REC-TYPE is 'U', executes a DB2 UPDATE on CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE setting TR_DESCRIPTION where TR_TYPE matches INPUT-REC-NUMBER. Abends on SQLCODE +100 (not found) or negative SQLCODE.
When INPUT-REC-TYPE is 'D', executes a DB2 DELETE from CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE where TR_TYPE matches INPUT-REC-NUMBER. Abends on SQLCODE +100 (not found) or negative SQLCODE.
Reads the next sequential record from TR-RECORD into WS-INPUT-REC. Sets LASTREC to 'Y' at end-of-file to terminate the processing loop.
On any error condition, displays the error message stored in WS-RETURN-MSG and sets RETURN-CODE to 4 to signal abnormal termination to the calling environment
After all records are processed (LASTREC = 'Y'), closes the TR-RECORD input file and exits the program

data_dependencies.description: TR-RECORD must be successfully opened (WS-INF-STATUS = '00') before any READ operations are attempted. No explicit guard prevents reads if open fails, which could cause a runtime error.

The LASTREC flag controls the main processing loop. It must be initialized to spaces and only set to 'Y' by the AT END clause of the READ statement. Premature or missed setting would cause infinite loops or skipped records.
The entire processing path depends on INPUT-REC-TYPE containing a valid value ('A', 'U', 'D', or '*'). Any other value triggers an abend via 9999-ABEND, halting all further processing.

All three database operations (INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE) depend on the DB2 SQL Communication Area (SQLCA) being properly included and populated after each EXEC SQL statement. SQLCODE is the primary indicator for success or failure routing.
The DB2 host variable declarations from DCLTRTYP must align with the CARDDEMO.TRANSACTION_TYPE table columns (TR_TYPE, TR_DESCRIPTION). Misalignment would cause SQL binding or runtime errors.

data_dependencies.dependency: INPUT-REC-NUMBER as primary key for UPDATE and DELETE
data_dependencies.description: Both UPDATE and DELETE operations use INPUT-REC-NUMBER as the WHERE clause key (TR_TYPE). If the value does not exist in the database, SQLCODE +100 is returned and the program abends rather than continuing.

data_dependencies.dependency: WS-INPUT-REC field layout matches file record layout
data_dependencies.description: The READ INTO WS-INPUT-REC depends on the physical file record layout matching the WS-INPUT-REC structure (1-byte type, 2-byte number, 50-byte description = 53 bytes total). A mismatch causes incorrect field parsing.

Records are processed strictly in the order they appear in the input file. There is no sorting or reordering, so dependent operations (e.g., inserting a record before updating it) must be ordered correctly in the input file.

The 9999-ABEND paragraph sets RETURN-CODE to 4 but does not issue STOP RUN, meaning execution continues after the abend handler. This creates a dependency risk where processing may continue after an error state.

error_handling.description: File open status is checked via WS-INF-STATUS after OPEN INPUT. A '00' status displays success; any other value displays 'OPEN FILE NOT OK' but does not halt execution or trigger an abend, meaning processing continues regardless of open failure. No explicit handling exists for READ errors beyond the AT END clause which sets LASTREC='Y' to terminate the read loop.

The EVALUATE on INPUT-REC-TYPE handles valid types 'A', 'U', 'D', and '*' (comment lines). Any unrecognized type falls into the WHEN OTHER branch, which builds an error message 'ERROR: TYPE NOT VALID' into WS-RETURN-MSG and performs the 9999-ABEND paragraph to display the message and set RETURN-CODE to 4.

After the SQL INSERT, SQLCODE is evaluated. SQLCODE=0 indicates success. SQLCODE<0 (SQL error) builds a message containing 'Error accessing: TRANSACTION_TYPE table. SQLCODE:' plus the formatted SQLCODE value into WS-RETURN-MSG and performs 9999-ABEND. No handling exists for SQLCODE=+100 (not-found) on insert, as it is not a relevant condition for inserts.

After the SQL UPDATE, SQLCODE is evaluated. SQLCODE=0 indicates success. SQLCODE=+100 (no rows found) builds 'No records found.' into WS-RETURN-MSG and performs 9999-ABEND. SQLCODE<0 builds a message with the table name and SQLCODE value into WS-RETURN-MSG and performs 9999-ABEND.

After the SQL DELETE, SQLCODE is evaluated. SQLCODE=0 indicates success. SQLCODE=+100 (no rows found) builds 'No records found.' into WS-RETURN-MSG and performs 9999-ABEND. SQLCODE<0 builds a message with the table name and SQLCODE value into WS-RETURN-MSG and performs 9999-ABEND.

All error paths converge at paragraph 9999-ABEND, which displays the contents of WS-RETURN-MSG and sets RETURN-CODE to 4 to signal a warning/error condition to the calling environment. Notably, 9999-ABEND does not issue a STOP RUN, so execution continues after the abend paragraph returns, which is a significant weakness — processing may proceed after a fatal error rather than terminating immediately.

Normal termination is handled by 2001-CLOSE-STOP, which closes the TR-RECORD file. The STOP RUN statement in 1001-READ-NEXT-RECORDS is placed after an EXIT statement, making it unreachable dead code. This means the program relies on falling through to end-of-procedure rather than an explicit STOP RUN for termination.
